slides.title: Position Sizing: How Much Can I Actually Lose?
lines: A trading lesson about stops, lots, ticks, leverage and portfolio heat.
Decide where the idea is wrong before deciding how large the trade should be.

slides.title: You like the setup. But is the contract too large?
lines: “My risk limit is $50, and one contract can lose $125.”
The correct position may be zero contracts — not a tighter arbitrary stop.

slides.title: Do these calculations before clicking buy/sell
lines: Add expected spread, commission and slippage, then recalculate effective exposure.

slides.title: Size derives from money at risk
lines: SIZE ≈ RISK $ / STOP RISK PER UNIT
Illustrative $50 risk budget; $5 per tick and 25-tick stop.
If minimum tradable size is 1 contract, the trade fails the risk test.

slides.title: Why one contract would exceed the plan
lines: Original instructional illustration — NOT observed price data.
1 contract × 25 ticks × $5 = $125 risk; planned budget is $50.

slides.title: A trade’s size is not its margin
lines: Total economic exposure to price moves.
Collateral required to maintain the trade.
Expected loss at stop under assumed fill conditions.
Combined risk from all related positions.
A high-leverage position can have a small posted margin and a large loss.

slides.title: A modest percentage is still real money
lines: Illustrative risk-budget choice, not a universal safe allocation.
Use the capital genuinely at risk, not an advertised prop notional balance.

slides.title: Volatility-aware does not mean guaranteed protection
lines: An ATR multiple scales proposed stop distance to recent range; choose multiplier in advance.
A chart level should invalidate the setup; ATR may buffer normal volatility.
Both affect dollar risk; change in stop distance requires a new size calculation.

slides.title: More entries mean new portfolio arithmetic
lines: TOTAL RISK = Σ STOP LOSS EACH LEG
Hypothetical legs on same idea before gaps and transaction costs.
Unrealised gains are not guaranteed funds for a new pyramid.

slides.title: Four tickets can be one macro trade
lines: Often expresses USD strength against its basket.
USD-long but also Japan-specific and carry-sensitive.
Count shared scenario loss, not just the number of symbols.

slides.title: Losses and recoveries are asymmetric
lines: Percentages measured against the pre-loss starting equity.
Aggressively increasing risk after a drawdown compounds vulnerability.

slides.title: Reward/risk alone does not establish an edge
lines: Hypothetical stable win rate and payoff before spreads and slippage.
A 2R target with fewer winners may have worse expectancy, not better.

slides.title: Stops can lose more than the model
lines: Real entry/exit prices differ from plotted mid-price.
Stops are execution instructions, not price guarantees.
Overnight and release gaps can jump beyond stop.
Market depth changes under stress; fills vary.

slides.title: Five checks that protect the account
lines: What makes this setup worth the risk?
Is full-size stop loss within budget incl costs?
What happens if correlated positions fail together?
When to stop, reduce or avoid trading?
Record estimates before the trade, not reconstructed after the result.

slides.title: What is the correct size?
lines: Does 1% risk × four USD trades mean diversified?
Sizing should survive plausible adverse fills and firm-specific limits.
